Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Pinnacle Financial Group Third Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, ladies and gentlemen, this conference is being recorded. In order to ask a question, you will need to press star one on your telephone keypad. We will pause momentarily to compile the Q&A roster.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to review Pinnacle Financial Group's results for the third quarter of 2024. With me this morning are John Reynolds, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; and Lisa Patel, Chief Risk Officer.

Before we begin, let me remind you that some of the statements we will be making today are forward-looking. These statements are based on current expectations and assumptions and are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of these factors.

I will now turn the call over to John Reynolds.

John Reynolds:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Pinnacle Financial Group delivered solid performance in the third quarter, demonstrating the strength of our diversified business model and our commitment to serving our customers.

Our key priorities for this year remain focused on:
1. Enhancing customer experience
2. Driving operational efficiency
3. Investing in strategic growth initiatives
4. Maintaining strong capital levels.

Now, I'd like to provide some highlights on our fee income breakdown across wealth management, investment banking, and cards, where we saw robust growth driven by market tailwinds and innovation; our net interest margin analysis, which benefited from asset repricing despite funding pressures; key strategic initiatives showing strong progress in digital and regional expansion; and revenue diversification efforts that have meaningfully shifted our mix toward more stable non-interest sources. These areas underscore our ability to execute through varying economic conditions.

I will now turn the call over to Michael Chen to discuss our financial results in more detail.

Michael Chen:
Thank you, John, and good morning. Pinnacle Financial Group reported net income of $1.5 billion for the third quarter, or $4.20 per share. Our results reflect strong revenue growth, disciplined expense management, and a healthy credit environment.

Net interest income increased 15% driven by higher interest rates and loan growth. Non-interest income benefited from fee momentum in key areas, though tempered by softer seasonal trading activity. We continue to maintain a strong capital position with a CET1 ratio of 13.2%. 

To give you more context on our performance, let me start with our net interest margin, or NIM, which expanded to 3.42% for the quarter—up 17 basis points year-over-year from 3.25% but holding steady sequentially. This outcome balances positive momentum from asset yields and portfolio shifts against ongoing funding cost challenges in a prolonged high-rate setting. Breaking it down, our NIM stems from net interest income of $1.28 billion on average earning assets of $148.5 billion. Annually, net interest income has climbed 12% to a $5.1 billion run rate, supported by 9% growth in earning assets and that 28 basis point margin lift year-over-year. Quarter-over-quarter, earning assets edged up 1.2% as we directed capital toward higher-return loans rather than securities given the yield curve inversion.

Asset yields improved 15 basis points to 5.25%, surpassing the 1.75% average for three-month SOFR. Loan repricing played a big role, with our $112.4 billion loan portfolio yielding 5.78%, up 22 basis points. C&I loans, at 42% of the book, gained from SOFR-tied adjustable rates, with fresh originations averaging 6.45% versus 6.12% prior. CRE stayed at 5.62%, but we trimmed $450 million in office loans, redirecting to multifamily and industrial segments at 6.1%. Securities yields rose 8 basis points to 3.95% on our $28.2 billion portfolio; we sped up paydowns on older agency MBS averaging 2.1% and redeployed $1.2 billion into corporates and munis at 4.6-4.8%, part of our ALM approach that nudged duration to 3.2 years while keeping LCR at 120%. Consumer mortgages trailed at 4.85% yield, with originations down 8% quarter-over-quarter to $2.1 billion amid 30-year rates near 7%.

On liabilities, costs rose 20 basis points to 1.95%, netting a 5 basis point drag. Deposits expanded 7% year-over-year to $132.8 billion, but mix shifted: cumulative deposit beta hit 48% over the 525 basis point Fed hike cycle, with marginal beta easing to 62% from 68% last quarter. Non-interest-bearing DDAs slipped to 22% of deposits from 25%, costing a mere 0.05%, while NOW and MMAs peaked at 2.85% for new funds. We cut FHLB advances 15% to $4.2 billion at 4.95% and brokered CDs by $800 million, prioritizing core funding. Ex-wholesale, core costs reached 1.72%, outperforming peers like Regions at 1.88% and Truist at 2.02%.

Regionally, our Southeast core markets, 55% of loans, saw NIM rise 25 basis points to 3.55% on C&I strength in Florida and Texas energy, with SOFR floors on revolvers at 7.2% and betas at 45% via our Pinnacle Premier program retaining 92% of affluent clients. Midwest markets, 25% of loans, managed 3.28% NIM amid Chicago CRE office pressures—NPAs up to 0.45%—offset by 6.3% yields in industrial logistics. National wholesale, 20%, shone with 7.1% yields from Pinnacle Capital leases on $8.5 billion.

We've countered with a dynamic AI pricing engine tied to FIS Profile for real-time MMA adjustments based on liquidity and peers, curbing beta by 5-7%; $3 billion in receive-fixed swaps at 3.85% locking 50 basis points spread with 95% effectiveness; and Pinnacle YieldGuard savings linked to loans, gathering 1.2 million digital deposits at 3.1% cost and 15% cross-sell to wealth. We see NIM stabilizing at 3.50-3.60% through year-end H2 before climbing into 2025 on 8-10% loan growth in high-yield C&I/CRE, 6% deposits with beta below 55%, and curve steepening—ranking top quartile per KBW, backed by 65/35 loan-to-deposit and 2.1x TCE coverage.

Next, our fee income truly stood out at $2.8 billion, up 18% year-over-year and 5% quarter-over-quarter, now 22% of total revenue and highlighting diversification in this rate regime. Wealth management led with $1.45 billion, up 22% YoY and 52% of fees—a 300 basis point shift—with AUM at $1.9 trillion from 12% organic inflows, especially HNW and ultra-HNW. Markets aided via 8% S&P gains, but ESG strategies doubled AUM to $250 billion on sovereign mandates like Norway's GPFG. Our Wealth360 AI robo-advisory lifted retention to 96%, cross-sell 15%, with 40% mass-affluent adding private banking. APAC surged 35% on China wealth transfers and Singapore JV; EMEA 15% despite UK FCA reviews, via Swiss inflows; North America 18% on 9-11% IRR private credit. We're advancing wealth orchestration—blending custody, lending, advisory—to push margins to 85 bps from 78, eyeing 90 bps with outcomes pricing.

Investment banking fees hit $850 million, up 25% YoY and 12% QoQ for 30% of fees, on $1.1 trillion global M&A per Dealogic—advisory up 40% to $150 billion equivalent, like a $45 billion tech carve-out similar to Broadcom-VMware. ECM jumped 60% on 15 IPOs/follow-ons, including $8 billion India renewables listing. DCM fees rose 10% to $12 billion underwriting at sub-5% yields. IBX platform's quantum optimization cut execution 20%, securing 60% top-client preference. Americas 55% on healthcare/software; EMEA 20% post-Brexit; APAC 25%, pivoting China ECM to ASEAN outbound. Margins up 250 bps to 32% under IFRS 15; ahead, Strategic Advisory Labs with McKinsey-style partners target doubled AI/biotech rankings.

Cards and payments added $500 million, up 12% YoY/8% QoQ or 18% share, on 14% volume to 2.1 billion transactions. Premium co-brands like Elite Rewards Visa Infinite grew acquisitions 25% via millennial campaigns. Interchange, 65% of fees, expanded 50 bps to 2.25% post-Durbin. Digital wallets at 55% via Apple Pay/BankPay drove 30% volume amid BNPL rivalry. Visa tokenization cut fraud 40%, enabling $100 million Shopify SME partnerships. U.S. +16% travel; Europe +10% vs PSD3; LatAm +28% Nubank-style in Brazil/Mexico. $200 million GenAI for rewards eyes 20% engagement lift, wallet share to 15% by 2025.

Overall, fees track to $11.5 billion full-year, up 16% with 2-3 points margin gains, outpacing JPM/Goldman peers.

Turning to key strategic initiatives, these are fueling growth across digital transformation, customer innovation, regional expansion, and responsible practices—linked revenues up 12% YoY to $2.8 billion or 28% of total, from 22%. UniDigital 3.0 got $1.2 billion YTD for AI personalization, cloud, APIs. UniAssist GenAI advisor covers 65% of 45 million retail clients, pushing digital transactions to 78%—up 15 points QoQ—and cutting service costs 22% by deflecting 1.2 million queries. Commercial APIs for PSD3/FedNow onboarded 450 fintechs like Plaid/Stripe for $450 million embedded fees, +35%. 85% core systems on AWS/Google Cloud save $180 million run-rate, STP at 97% for ISO 20022.

OneUni ecosystem raised cross-sell to 4.8 products/customer. Retail deposits +9% to $320 billion via 4.75% digital savings matching Ally/SoFi at 2.45% NIM post-50bps cut. UniWealth AI AUM over $50 billion with 25% inflows, ESG beating MSCI by 180bps; NPS 72, churn 3.1% vs industry 5-7%.

North America (55% profits) added 2.2 million digital accounts post-SVB; CET1 13.2% aided $5 billion CRE restructures at 15% discount. Europe IB fees +18% to €1.1 billion via 25% German neobank stake for Digital Euro. APAC +22%, deposits +14% to $150 billion; ₹10,000 crore green bonds tap $500 billion sustainable market. China JV steady at 8% growth.

Risk/ESG: Basel IV RWA cut 5% via IFRS 9 for 14-15% RoTE; 42% loans sustainability-linked per TCFD/SFDR; net-zero Scope 1/2 down 28%, $3 billion green deposits ahead of HSBC/BNP.

These deliver 32% digital revenue growth, peak engagement, resilient profile—FY24 target $11.5-12 billion, 10-12% EPS.

On revenue diversification, non-interest now 48% of total vs 39% two years ago, buffering NII cyclicality at 3.42% NIM down 12bps QoQ from betas at Fed 5.25-5.50%. Wealth AUM +22% to $1.2 trillion on S&P +18% YTD/HNW inflows; advisory/custody +28% to $1.8 billion or 15% revenue via GlobalWealth AI for ETF/ESG rebalancing—retention 96%, cross-sell 4.2, CLV +15%. APAC +35% DBS JV; EMEA +12% ESG at 28% AUM.

Payments +32% to $2.4 billion/20% revenue on 4.2 billion GlobalPay transactions +45%, B2B tickets +8%. APIs in Stripe/Adyen for RTP/FedNow; Visa/MC tokenization -40% fraud, +$300 million interchange. Brazil Pix 51% stake +55%, 12% share; U.S. sweeps stabilize beta at 45%.

CIB +19% to $1.6 billion: advisory +25% on $180 billion/45 M&A deals like $25 billion bank merger; DCM $120 billion on 95bps spreads. Corda blockchain trade finance -30% costs, $150 million Middle East pipeline.

Diversify 2025: $2.5 billion cloud/Temenos migration, Snowflake/Databricks 95% upselling accuracy +22% fees; RegTech -18% compliance. Added 450bps non-int growth, $6.2 billion to $4.85 EPS/14.2% ROTCE +180bps; beta 0.65 vs NII 1.2; CCAR 200bps shock -5% revenue.

Regions: North America 55%, APAC 22% +6 points, EMEA 15%, LatAm 8%. Middle East geopolitics -5% CIB, <2% loans. GlobalOne neobank 2.5 million users/1.5% margins.

Targets 55% non-int by 2026, $10 billion embedded/wealth; +18% wallet share; Q4 25-28% growth on M&A/payments. 12-15% EPS CAGR.

We are pleased with the progress we are making on our strategic initiatives, and we remain confident in our ability to deliver sustainable value for our shareholders.

Operator, we are now ready to open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. [Operator Instructions] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide some color on loan growth expectations going forward?

John Reynolds:
Good morning, John. Thanks for the question. We're projecting 8-10% loan growth for the full year, skewed toward higher-yielding C&I and select CRE like multifamily and industrial, where we're seeing strong demand in Southeast markets such as Florida and Texas energy sectors. We've been selective, de-risking office exposure by reallocating $450 million while maintaining robust originations at 6.45% yields on new C&I via SOFR structures. National lease financing through Pinnacle Capital continues to deliver 7.1% returns on our $8.5 billion book. Regionally, APAC and LatAm expansions support this, with India green lending and Brazil digital stacks adding momentum. Customer cross-sell from our OneUni ecosystem and embedded finance partnerships are key drivers, alongside Pinnacle YieldGuard tying deposits to commitments. This positions us well for NIM accretion into 2025, even with potential Fed cuts.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Davis with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Emily Davis:
Good morning. What is your outlook for deposit costs and betas?

Michael Chen:
Good morning, Emily. Deposit betas have stabilized, with cumulative at 48% over the full hike cycle and marginal now at 62%, down from 68% late last year—a sign of moderation. Core funding costs are at 1.72%, below peers, thanks to our 22% non-interest-bearing DDA base and real-time AI pricing engine that's curbed creep by 5-7 points. Wholesale reductions in FHLB and CDs further help. Looking ahead, we expect 6% deposit growth with betas under 55%, supported by Premier relationship banking retaining 92% HNW clients and high-yield digital products like YieldGuard at competitive APYs. Diversification into payments and wealth shields us, with sweeps stabilizing at 45%. In a 50-75 bps cut scenario, this supports NIM at 3.50-3.60% through H2 before expansion.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Barclays. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Good morning. Can you discuss the impact of commercial real estate on your loan portfolio?

Lisa Patel:
Good morning, David. CRE remains manageable at about 25% of our loan book, with yields steady at 5.62%. We've proactively de-risked by $450 million in office, shifting to multifamily and industrial at 6.1%, and completed $5 billion in restructurings at 15% discounts using our strong 13.2% CET1 buffer. NPAs ticked up modestly to 0.45% in Midwest office stress areas like Chicago, but overall credit quality is healthy—42% of loans now sustainability-linked with KPIs under TCFD/SFDR. Basel IV optimizations and IFRS 9 models cut RWAs 5%, and our derisked exposure under 2% in volatile regions like Middle East. Stress tests show resilience, with diversification absorbing shocks. We're focused on relationship-driven underwriting and tech for early detection.

Operator:
There are no further questions at this time. I'd like to turn the conference back over to John Reynolds for any closing remarks.

John Reynolds:
Thank you for your interest in Pinnacle Financial Group. We appreciate you joining us today. We look forward to speaking with you again next quarter.

Operator:
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
